items.text: Morgan Stanley sponsors deferred cash-based compensation and stock-based compensation programs for financial advisors in the Wealth Management segment that generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions, which function to retain advisors.
items.quote: The Firm sponsors a number of deferred cash-based compensation programs and stock-based compensation programs for current and former employees, including financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.

items.text: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.quote: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's compensation programs, aimed in part at attracting and retaining top talent, include annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.
items.quote: We provide responsible and effective compensation programs that reinforce our values and culture through four key objectives: deliver pay for sustainable performance, attract and retain top talent, align with shareholder interests and mitigate excessive risk-taking. In addition to salaries, these programs (which vary by location) include annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is increasing the cash component of its advisor compensation, describing the changes as supporting its overall investment into its financial advisors and simplifying its compensation program.
items.quote: As previously announced, we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings. While there will be some transitional costs, these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: In the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management representatives (advisors).
items.quote: in the current quarter, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management representatives.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes itself as paying for performance, with advisor/partner upside coming through compensation over many years (hence tenure matters) and total return in stock ownership, a critical part of partner compensation.
items.quote: We pay for performance. Performance comes in sort of the upside for our partners comes in two forms. One is through compensation over many years, which is why tenure matters. Of course, total return in stock ownership, which is, as you know, a critical part of partner compensation.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors, adhering to a more traditional (deferred-compensation-based) approach, and is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

cells.reason: The passages describe Morgan Stanley's advisor retention mechanisms: deferred/stock-based compensation with vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions, cash compensation increases, pay-for-performance and stock ownership, and its decision not to use retention bonuses.
